summary: PeptAI is an autonomous AI agent platform for peptide drug discovery targeting three GPCRs (KISS1R, OX2R, GLP-1R benchmark), operating an eight-gate computational pipeline followed by one wet-lab validation gate. Lead candidates for KISS1R (C1-01, C1-02) and OX2R (OX2R-004, OX2R-004-S1) have cleared all eight computational gates and are queued for wet-lab validation at Adaptyv Bio and Ginkgo Bioworks. The project is funded via a $50K Ignition Sale of the $PEPTAI ERC-20 token on BIO Protocol, with all gate decisions published on-chain via Molecule Labs.

content_blocks.title: Cover / Document Metadata
content_blocks.content: PeptAI Whitepaper, Version 5, April 2026. Programmes: KISS1R, OX2R, GLP-1R (benchmark). Token: $PEPTAI ERC-20 on Base, Ignition Sale via BIO Protocol. Tagline: 'An autonomous AI agent for peptide drug discovery with programmatic on-chain funding. Eight computational gates, one wet-lab gate, every decision published.'

content_blocks.title: Abstract — Platform Overview and Current Status
content_blocks.content: PeptAI operates a universal eight-gate computational pipeline: structure prediction (G1), binding pose generation (G2-G3), molecular dynamics (G4-G5), ADMET screening (G6), physicochemical profiling (G7), selectivity/safety (G8), and one wet-lab experimental validation gate (G9). Gates 1–8 are fully autonomous; Gate 9 is wet lab only. The pipeline is target-agnostic with target-specific calibration parameters. GLP-1R is the benchmark target. KISS1R leads C1-01 and C1-02 (from a 10-candidate library) and OX2R leads OX2R-004 (18-residue agonist) plus stabilized variant OX2R-004-S1 have cleared all eight computational gates. These candidates are queued for wet-lab validation at Adaptyv Bio and Ginkgo Bioworks. Key stats: 9 pipeline gates (1–8 autonomous), 3 GPCR programmes, $50K Ignition Sale, 10M $PEPTAI fixed supply.

content_blocks.title: Section 1 — Lead Programmes and Therapeutic Rationale
content_blocks.content: Three GPCR programmes: (1) KISS1R — indication: idiopathic hypogonadotropic hypogonadism / fertility. Status: 2 leads (C1-01, C1-02) cleared all 8 gates against PDB 8XGO. Adaptyv BLI + Ginkgo cAMP HTRF queued. (2) OX2R — indication: ADHD / narcolepsy via orexin agonism. Status: OX2R-004 (18-residue agonist) + variant OX2R-004-S1 cleared computational feasibility. Adaptyv binding queued. (3) GLP-1R — metabolic medicine, calibration target. Reference panel: semaglutide, liraglutide, tirzepatide. $45B 2024 revenue. Calibrates platform performance. Differentiator: first AI drug discovery pipeline where every gate decision is published on-chain in real time, IP-NFT minting tied to experimentally verified milestones, and community funding tied to verified experimental outcomes.

content_blocks.title: Section 1.2 — Why AI Agents Now (Technology Enablers)
content_blocks.content: Three convergent developments cited: (1) Structure prediction at near-atomic resolution — AlphaFold2 and Boltz2 produce binding-pose predictions at Å-scale accuracy on receptor-peptide complexes. (2) Molecular dynamics at scale — LiteFold's native MD engine enables microsecond-equivalent sampling of peptide-GPCR complexes at high-throughput cost. (3) Agentic orchestration — LLM-orchestrated multi-tool workflows compress hypothesis-to-result cycles from months to hours. Supporting literature: ML-produced novel GLP-1R/GCGR dual agonists (Puszkarska et al., Nature Chemistry 2024); AI-driven de novo design of ultra-long-acting GLP-1R agonists (Wei et al., 2025); first AI-designed drug completed Phase 2a (Nature Medicine 2025).

content_blocks.title: Section 2 — Nine-Gate Pipeline Architecture with Thresholds and Status
content_blocks.content:
Gate | Description | Tool(s) | Threshold | Status
G1 | Target Structure | AlphaFold DB / Boltz2 | pLDDT > 0.65 (helical core, residues 7–26) | LIVE
G2 | Conformational Sampling | LiteFold MD | ≥2 clusters, dominance > 50% | LIVE
G3 | Binding Pose | Boltz2 + PDB 3IOL | Contact conservation > 60%, BSA > 800Å², clash ≤ 5 | LIVE
G4 | Binding Affinity | PRODIGY | ΔG < −10 kcal/mol (GPCR) | PARTIAL → LIVE
G5 | MD Stability | LiteFold MD | RMSD < 3Å, min RMSF residues 17–22 | LIVE
G6 | ADMET + Stability | PROSPERous + QSAR | t½ > 2 hrs, ≤ 2 cleavage sites; ADMET within injectable bounds | LIVE
G7 | Physicochemical | OpenSol + AGGRESCAN | Solubility > 1 mg/mL, low aggregation, IC50 > 500 nM | LIVE
G8 | Selectivity + Safety | ToxinPred3 + Boltz2 | ΔΔG > 1.4 kcal/mol, non-toxic | LIVE
G9 | Experimental Binding | SPR / BLI · Adaptyv | Kd < 1 µM hit / < 100 nM lead | WET LAB ONLY

Note on G6: ADMET profile includes estimated plasma half-life, Caco-2 permeability proxy, hERG and CYP3A4 risk assessment, BBB Score, and renal clearance estimate. ADMET predictions are directional rather than quantitative for this MW range.

content_blocks.title: Section 2.2–2.3 — Calibration and Gate 0 Autonomous Self-Calibration
content_blocks.content: Gate thresholds are empirically grounded against a reference panel of known GLP-1R agonists and negative controls. Positive controls pass, negative controls fail, off-target peptides are correctly flagged. Gate 0 is a pre-pipeline step: the agent autonomously establishes a baseline for the target class using BIOS to identify reference compounds, then queries ChEMBL by target ID for structured binding data (Kd/EC50) for known binders and non-binders. Minimum panel: one confirmed agonist + one confirmed non-binder. Panel is run through Gates 1–8 to compute per-gate baseline (mean ± SD across Class A reference compounds). All downstream candidate scores expressed as Z-scores: Z = (score − class mean) / class SD. Gate 4 caveat: PRODIGY ΔG values are unreliable in absolute terms for peptide-GPCR contacts (model trained on protein-protein interfaces). ΔG is used for relative ranking (Z-score vs. panel), not converted to predicted Kd. Absolute Kd prediction deferred until Adaptyv Bio SPR data accumulates.

content_blocks.title: Section 3 — Generative Discovery Engine and Phase Roadmap
content_blocks.content:
Current state (Phase 1): scoring machine — human proposes sequence, agent evaluates. Phase 1.5 converts to generative loop: system generates sequences, scores them, learns from experimental results, generates better candidates. Fitness function has two components: (1) Computational fitness (now) — gate scores G1–G8 combined into composite ranking; internally consistent but not yet externally validated against experimental binding data. (2) Experimental fitness (unlocked by Gate 9a) — Kd from SPR at Adaptyv; once 10–15 paired computational-experimental measurements available, fitness function calibrated to weight each gate by actual predictive power.

Phase roadmap:
- Phase 1 (Now/Current): Pipeline live. Agent-evaluated scoring of human-proposed candidates.
- Phase 1.5 (Q2 2026): Calibration. Agent self-calibration against ChEMBL reference panels.
- Phase 2A (Q2–Q3 2026): Gate 9a SPR data. Fitness model v1: predicts Kd from gate scores.
- Phase 2B (Q3 2026): Fitness model v1 validated. Generative candidate design unlocked.
- Phase 2C (Q1 2027): First SPR hits confirmed. In-vivo PK/PD begins.
- Phase 3 (2027+): In-vivo signal confirmed. De-risked asset and licensing possibility.

content_blocks.title: Section 4 — Wet Lab Strategy: Two Parallel Tracks
content_blocks.content:
Track A — Natural-AA Candidates (Adaptyv Bio, weeks 3–4):
- Synthesised and assayed end-to-end at Adaptyv Bio.
- Reference peptides: KP-10 (KISS1R reference), OX2R-004 (OX2R parent), Orexin-B (OX2R native ligand reference).
- Purpose: establish binding baselines and calibrate Adaptyv assay platform before higher-cost ncAA peptides.
- Cost: ~$240–440. Lead time: 3–4 weeks. Output: binding baseline.

Track B — ncAA Candidates (Specialty CRO → Adaptyv → Ginkgo, weeks 7–9):
- Lead candidates with non-canonical amino acid modifications: D-amino acids, Nω-methyl-Arg, azaGly, N-acetylation.
- Synthesis at JPT, Bachem, or GenScript.
- Routed to Adaptyv Bio for BLI binding and selectivity.
- Top binders advance to Ginkgo Bioworks for cAMP HTRF functional assays.
- 3 vendors. Lead time: 7–9 weeks. Output: design vs. nature comparison.

content_blocks.title: Section 4.2 — Planned Partner Network
content_blocks.content:
Partner | Role | Gate | Phase

Bachem | GMP synthesis scale-up | Scale-up | Phase 3

content_blocks.title: Section 5 — On-Chain Architecture
content_blocks.content: Two infrastructure layers: (1) OpenClaw (agent runtime) — open-source framework for autonomous research agents; each programme runs on dedicated OpenClaw instance with own memory, session history, communication channel; orchestrates LiteFold, BIOS; publishes to Molecule Labs. Architecture is experimental, ~3 months of development across two major revision cycles. (2) BIO Protocol (funding & governance) — $PEPTAI token (ERC-20 on Base), Safe multisig treasury, Ignition Sale mechanism; funds allocated to agent wallets via Privy's programmatic wallet infrastructure. Publication surface: all pipeline runs publish to Molecule Labs with sequence, gate scores, tool identification, PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED/PARTIAL status, timestamp, on-chain hash. IP-NFT via Molecule: minting tied to dynamically validated candidates (not static proposals). Funding: $25K initial R&D budget funds wet-lab campaign; ongoing R&D from DAO Allocation (40% of total supply); no separate follow-on raise, no milestone-gated unlock schedule.

content_blocks.content:

content_blocks.title: Section 7 — Risk Factors
content_blocks.content:
Scientific risks: (1) Computational–experimental correlation may be lower than expected — if gate scores do not predict experimental Kd, Phase 2 fitness model will have poor accuracy and generative loop will not converge. Mitigation: calibration panel data and Bits to Binders 2026 benchmark provide prior evidence for G5 predictive power. (2) Phase 1 optimises for binding affinity only — a computationally/experimentally good sequence may still prove balanced rather than biased; Phase 2 Ginkgo functional assays required before bias can be assessed; timeline H2 2026 at earliest. (3) Non-canonical amino acid synthesis risk — lead candidates contain ncAA modifications (D-amino acids, Nω-methyl-Arg, azaGly, N-terminal acetylation) requiring specialist synthesis; azaGly7 in C1-02 with adjacent Thr5 is the most discriminating cross-vendor question.

Execution risks: (1) Gate 9a timing uncertainty — Adaptyv Bio SPR scheduling is single most critical dependency on Phase 2 roadmap; delays fitness model, generative loop, and all downstream milestones. Mitigation: early engagement with Adaptyv Bio; Track A proceeds in parallel. (2) Agent infrastructure is experimental — depends on OpenRouter (LLM inference), LiteFold (MD); service outages, rate limits, API changes can halt progress; architecture revised twice in first month. Mitigation: instances can be forked, reconfigured, relaunched with snapshots.

key_findings: KISS1R programme: 2 lead candidates (C1-01, C1-02) from a 10-candidate library have cleared all 8 computational gates against PDB 8XGO; queued for Adaptyv Bio BLI and Ginkgo cAMP HTRF wet-lab validation.
OX2R programme: OX2R-004 (18-residue agonist) and stabilized variant OX2R-004-S1 have cleared computational feasibility (all 8 gates); queued for Adaptyv Bio binding assay.
GLP-1R serves as benchmark/calibration target only (reference panel: semaglutide, liraglutide, tirzepatide); no novel GLP-1R candidates reported.
No wet-lab experimental data has been generated yet — Gate 9 (Kd < 1 µM hit / < 100 nM lead by SPR/BLI) is pending; all current evidence is computational.
Eight-gate computational pipeline is fully live (Gates 1–8 LIVE, Gate 4 PARTIAL→LIVE); tools include AlphaFold2/Boltz2, LiteFold MD, PRODIGY, PROSPERous, AGGRESCAN, ToxinPred3.
Gate 4 (PRODIGY ΔG) acknowledged as unreliable in absolute terms for peptide-GPCR contacts; used only for relative Z-score ranking vs. reference panel, not absolute Kd prediction.

Lead candidates contain non-canonical amino acid modifications (D-amino acids, Nω-methyl-Arg, azaGly, N-acetylation) requiring specialist synthesis; azaGly7 in C1-02 with adjacent Thr5 flagged as highest synthesis risk.
Fitness function is currently computational only (G1–G8 composite); experimental fitness (Kd from SPR) requires 10–15 paired measurements to calibrate gate weights — not yet available.

Phase roadmap: Phase 1 (current, scoring), Phase 1.5 (Q2 2026, ChEMBL self-calibration), Phase 2A (Q2–Q3 2026, Gate 9a SPR data), Phase 2B (Q3 2026, generative design unlocked), Phase 2C (Q1 2027, first SPR hits + in-vivo PK/PD), Phase 3 (2027+, licensing).
Funding: $50K Ignition Sale via BIO Protocol; $25K seeds initial R&D (wet-lab campaign), $25K as liquidity on Aerodrome; ongoing R&D governed by DAO Allocation (40% of 10M token supply).
IP-NFT minting via Molecule Labs tied to dynamically validated candidates (not static proposals); all gate decisions published on-chain in real time.
Agent infrastructure is experimental (~3 months development, 2 major revision cycles); depends on external services (OpenRouter, LiteFold) with acknowledged outage/rate-limit risks.

TRL assessment: project is at approximately TRL 2–3 — computational pipeline validated against reference compounds, lead candidates identified computationally, but no experimental binding data yet generated.
